title: Excavations in Palestine, 1934-5: 'Anata and Ras el Kharrube
author: (round-up; soundings directed by A. Bergman and E. P. Blair)
location_note: 'Anata village hill and Ras el Kharrube (Anathoth); no map references; placed by name.
reading: full (the span includes the map figure on p. 195)
notes: January 1936 soundings for the identification of Anathoth. 'Anata: five soundings, pottery Hellenistic (perhaps Persian) to Arabic. Ras el Kharrube: five pits, Early Iron II to Byzantine pottery, a wall on the north side.

features.subtype: kokim tomb with unfinished loculi; later used as store room and as cistern
features.period: Hellenistic (cutting); Roman re-use as store room
features.quote: a Hellenistic tomb was discovered of the kokim type, the loculi

features.subtype: the kokim tomb re-used as a cistern
features.quote: in Byzantine and Early Arabic, as a cistern

features.subtype: two-storey cistern, the lower one roofed with rough stones
features.period: not dated (site pottery Early Iron II to Byzantine)
features.quote: One proved to be a two-story cistern
